Abu Asad Bhuiyan and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Abu Taher Bhuiyan others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This is defendants appeal by leave against the judgment dated November 5, 2000 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1434 of 1999 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated March 24, 1999 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 6 of 1998 dismissing the same upon affirming the judgment and decree dated January 22, 1998 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Monohardi, Narsingdi in Title Suit No. 64 of 1996 decreeing the same against the defendant Nos. 1-9 on contest and ex parte against the rest declaring the title of the plaintiffs in respect of the land in suit and that the record of rights, i.e. SA and RS khatians, prepared in the name of defendants' predecessor Abu Sufian was wrong. 

 2. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that Jagadish Chandra and Ramesh Chandra permanently made settlement of the land in suit to Firoz Bhuiyan, predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 10 by the Hukumnama dated 10th Kartick, 1344 BS and father of the defendant Nos. 1-9, Abu Sufian put his signature on the Hukumnama as a witness, that Abu Sufian was a clever man and though was not ever the owner and possessor of the land in suit, yet in collusion with the survey officials, managed to get his name recorded in the SA khatian in respect of half of the land taken settlement by Firoz Bhuiyan, that at the time of preparation of the RS record defendant Nos. 1-9's predecessor also got the record of right prepared in his name in respect of 8 annas share on the basis of SA record, that on the basis of the record of right, particularly on the basis of RS record, defendants raised claim in respect of the land taken settlement by Firoz Bhuiyan and that in that state of the matter plaintiffs upon obtaining the copy of the SA and RS record came to know about the preparation of the said records in respect of the land in suit wrongly in the name of the defendant Nos. 1-9 predecessor Hence the suit for declaration of title simplicities. 

 12. The learned Counsel has submitted that although Hukumnama was in the name of Firoz Bhuiyan but from the facts on record it is seen that settlement was taken for the benefit of both the brothers i.e. Firoz Bhuiyan and Abu Sufian who were living jointly and that settlement was taken with the income of joint family. It may be mentioned that the contention as to taking settlement with the income of the joint family has not been established from the side of the defendants. It has also been submitted since Firoz Bhuiyan allowed his brother Abu Sufian to possess half of the land taken settlement by the Hukumnama and during Firoz Bhuiyan's lifetime Abu Sufian constructed huts in half of the land taken settlement and was hying there and that as during Firoz Bhuiyan's lifetime SA record was prepared in the name of Firoz Bhuiyan and Abu Sufian recording 8 arenas share each and as no exception was taken about the preparation of the SA record by Firoz Bhuiyan, the entirety of the facts mentioned hereinbefore thus clearly show that settlement was taken the benefit of Firoz Bhuiyan and Abu Sufian. It is also the contention of the learned Counsel for the appellants that as exception was not taken in respect of the SA record, preparation of the RS record in the light of the SA record in the name of Firoz Bhuiyan and Abu Sufian noting equal share in the land listed in RS khatian cannot be considered wrong, that evidence led by the parties in the suit clearly shows that Abu Sufian and after him. his heirs are in possession of half of the lapd taken settlement by the Hukumnama and hence claim of title in.the entire land of Hukumnama by the plaintiffs is not sustainable in law, that High Court Division in the background of the evidence on record held both the plaintiffs and the defendants are in possession and title being in favour of Firoz alone the possession should be construed the possession of Firoz alone and Abu Sufian may be treated as "intruder" is not well founded in law since Abu Sufian as from the date of settlement i.e. from 1344 BS, possessed the land and the SA record was prepared in his name, as such, he cannot be considered intruder. The learned Counsel continues that Abu Sufian with, the consent of Firoz Bhuiyan spent money and, built huts in the land in suit and lived there and thereafter defendants are living and that as plaintiffs are in possession of half of the total land taken settlement by the Hukumnama the same implies That the plaintiffs are not in possession of the other half and, as such suit as framed seeking mere declaration of title is not maintainable. The learned Counsel further submits that Firoz Bhuiyan waved his right in respect of half of the land taken settlement by the Hukumnama by allowing Abu Sufian to possess half of the land of the total quantity of land taken settlement by the Hukumnama dated 10th Kartick, 1344 BS and thus Firoz Bhuiyan lost his right in half of the land taken settlement by the Hukumnama by waiver, estoppel and acquiescence. The learned Counsel lastly, submits that finding of the High Court Division that both parties are in possession was not challenged by the plaintiffs and, as such, the said finding alone is sufficient for the purpose of upholding the contention of the defendants that the suit as framed is not maintainable or, in other words, suit seeking mere declaration of title is not maintainable.
